current.title: Right stylohyoid ligament · CT orientation · draft
current.body: Distinguish the stylohyoid ligament from the temporal styloid process and stylohyoid muscle. Acquired CT can show mineralised portions of the stylohyoid complex; these do not outline every part of a normal nonossified ligament.
bullets: Elongation or mineralisation can be incidental. Imaging alone does not establish Eagle syndrome or explain symptoms.

current.title: Trochlea of right superior oblique · CT orientation · draft
current.body: Locate the side-specific superior-oblique tendon pulley in the superomedial orbit. Acquired CT may show mineralisation at the tendon turn; an incidental focus is not the complete cartilage, tendon or muscle.
bullets: Calcification alone neither diagnoses systemic disease nor excludes injury or a foreign body.
The donor surface supplies no CT attenuation, calcific deposit, tissue-thickness measurement or validated patient boundary.
